Whats up fellow voaters and preppers!

No matter what kind of situation you're preparing for, you don't have to buy every single survival gadget, gizmo and gun. I've always been a big supporter of personal finance, fiscal responsibility, and preparing for disaster. Those things all sort of work hand-in-hand. Practicing a budget and having fiscal responsibility is the best way to be prepared for the civilized world, just like having food and shelter is the best way to prepare for the uncivilized world.

People get carried away though - I have some friends who seem to be in an arms race for war preparation. They stockpile weapons and ammo like they're getting ready to militarize a small nation. Some of my friends have "first aid kids" that are actually tier 3 trauma kits for gunshot wounds, and then they forget to stock pepto bismol and antibiotics. They seem to be forgetting that they're preparing for a natural disaster or supply shortage, instead of a vacation to a war torn nation-state where they will need to kill their neighbors. Yes, that sort of thing COULD happen, as it has in the past, but as a family man, I'm going to be hunkered down, not preparing to fight soldiers in the streets.

So in my family we keep things pretty simply as far as being prepared goes:

Make sure all of our doors and windows can be locked up tight.
Some lumber out back to board things up if necessary.
Keeping a handgun and a shotgun in the house with a couple hundred rounds stocked.
6 month food supply
6 month water supply
Warm bedding and blankets
Lots of books and games
Harmonica, guitar, small drum.
Learning materials to engage your mind like math, science and foreign language
Medicine for a household. Antibiotics, anti-acids, vitamins, Advil/Tylenol, some bandages.

Maybe I'm the schmuck here, but I'm not going to spend my life preparing for a war that never happens, or training myself to live in the deep woods permanently. I'm happy to enjoy my family in our current society and try to prepare for a natural disaster or supply chain disruption.
You Don't Need To Be The Most Prepared, Just More Prepared Than Most
It's not very common that I run into a prepper that isn't way into firearms. I don't think your a schmuck, you are probably far more into realistic preparedness than most.

You're not a schmuck. No one can be completely prepared for every possibility. I think many people get into prepping because for whatever reason they suddenly realize that the systems they rely on everyday are vulnerable and could fail without warning. Fear doesn't lead to good planning or decision making so they end up making a lot of plans and purchases based on a sense of extreme urgency and whatever their worst-case scenario is. Apocalyptic fiction doesn't help much with making cool-headed risk assessments.

I certainly started that way (back in the dinosaur era even before the y2k panic.) I've watched a lot of expensive supplies expire unused. 18 years later and the unsustainable system keeps chugging along. I still think we're riding in a hand basket on our way to nowhere nice but I have no idea when or if the SHTF will occur. It's good to prepare but the most useful preps aren't very sexy. Find a place to live where you could ride out a storm, but that you can also afford and enjoy for years even if nothing happens. Store what you use and use what you store. Don't imagine a SHTF scenario as an escape from whatever irritates or dissatisfies you today.

These days it's interesting to watch world events but I don't get very ruffled by the latest scare about terrorism, pandemic or economic collapse. I've thought about the implications of most foreseeable disasters and I think I generally know what to do and have some supplies to work with. I do continue to prepare and I try to store a years worth of daily consumables and supplies for a few likely contingencies. I've accepted that I'm going to need to throw away a couple hundred dollars worth of expired antibiotics etc every few years and I've come to consider that as a sign that I've been blessed not to need them, much like recharging an expired fire extinguisher.

I know I'll never be completely ready but I think I'm generally ready enough. As the saying goes about stocks: the market can remain irrational far longer than you can remain solvent. Prepping is a lifestyle. You have to enjoy the now without robbing yourself to prepare for a future that may never come to pass. Things like gardening and beer brewing are fun whatever happens. An energy efficient home that you own is a good investment even if the system doesn't crash in your lifetime. Shooting and reloading is a fun hobby and you may need effective self defense at any time without TSHTF. Moderation in all things, (including moderation.)

Holy crap I'd forgotten about y2k. Remember the fever around it? It was like people were actually hoping the whole system would just shut down. What's worse is in my opinion it seems like people are even more excited about it now. "Can't wait for the zombies!"

I think the whole thing would be like a very serious shock to most people. It's all fun and games until the clean underwear runs out. Then the clean water. Then the idea of ever being clean again. Then the toilet paper. At that point, nothing is fun ever again.

Yeah. It's always unsettling to run into people who seem to be looking forward to "the end of the world as we know it." I remember people who went thousands and thousands of dollars into debt buying fallout shelters and huge stocks of freeze dried food. I wonder how many of them abandoned the idea of prepping in embarrassment afterwards.

It's kinda interesting that something similar doesn't seem to show up on prepper radar these days. Society is so much more computerized now. We talk about an EMP but what if the computers started giving the wrong answers like stuxnet? We're already at cyber war with whoever hacked OPM and stole every federal employee's fingerprints, social security numbers and blackmail-able info.
